items.prose: You are on main and want to start work on a new branch, fx-carry, straight away.
items.question: Which single command makes the branch and puts you on it?

options.why: That makes the label but leaves HEAD on main. Your next commit would land on main.
Without `-c`, switch only moves to a branch that already exists. fx-carry does not.
Merging brings a branch in. It cannot make one.

feedback.correct: `-c` creates the branch, and switch moves HEAD onto it.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. You need to create the branch and move HEAD in one step.

explain.text: `git switch -c fx-carry` makes a label at the current commit and points HEAD at it. Your next commit then moves fx-carry, not main.

items.prose: Six commits in a line. main points at c3; momentum points at c6, and HEAD is on momentum.

params.aria: Commit graph: circles are commits, arrows point to parents, labels point at commits

items.question: How many commits does main contain?

feedback.correct: From c3 the arrows reach c2 and c1: three commits.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Follow the arrows back from main only.

byKey.all: You counted momentum's commits as well. Arrows point backwards, so from c3 you never reach c4 to c6.
byKey.tip: main points at one commit but contains every commit behind it.

explain.text: main contains c1, c2 and c3. momentum contains all six, so the first three are on both branches. A merge of momentum into main would be a fast-forward.

items.prose: On main you run `git merge fx-carry`.

params.aria: Commit graph: circles are commits, arrows point to parents, labels point at commits

items.question: What does git do?

options.text: Makes a merge commit with parents c4 and c6

options.why: Sliding main to c6 would drop c3 and c4. A fast-forward needs main directly behind the branch.
A conflict needs the same lines changed on both sides. The picture shows history, not lines; a split alone is no conflict.

options.text: Moves fx-carry to a merge commit
options.why: A merge moves the branch you are on. HEAD is on main.

feedback.correct: Both sides have new commits, so git joins them with a merge commit.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Is main directly behind fx-carry?

explain.text: main has c3 and c4 that fx-carry lacks, and fx-carry has c5 and c6 that main lacks. So git makes a merge commit with two parents, c4 and c6. main moves to it; fx-carry stays on c6.

items.prose:


items.question: How many commits were made on value-signal before it was merged?

feedback.correct: The right-hand lane holds three commits.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the stars in the right-hand lane.

byKey.with-merge: You counted the merge commit too. It was made on main, to join the lanes.
byKey.all: You counted every commit in the picture. Only the right-hand lane is value-signal's.

explain.text: The `| *` lines are the right-hand lane: 41c09d8, 0be7c55 and c2a91f4. 9d6b310 is in main's lane, and 7f3e1a2 joins the two. 5e8a0c1 comes before the split, so it is on both.

items.prose: You are on main and merge the branch slippage. params.py now holds:
items.question: Which value is on main?

options.why: That is in the half ending >>>>>>> slippage, so it came from the slippage branch.
git never combines numbers. Each half is one branch's version of the line.

feedback.correct: The half under <<<<<<< HEAD is the branch you are on, main.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. HEAD is the branch you are on.

explain.text: HEAD is main, and its half runs from `<<<<<<< HEAD` to `=======`. So main says 2 and slippage says 3. You decide which belongs in the finished file.

items.prose: config.yaml has six lines. In each case, main and a branch each make one edit since they split.
items.question: Select all that apply: which cases stop the merge with a conflict?

options.text: Both change line 3, to different values
main changes line 3; the branch changes line 4
main changes line 2; the branch changes line 5
options.why: Lines 3 and 4 are untouched between the edits, so git takes each edit from where it was made.

options.text: main edits config.yaml; the branch only adds a new file, notes.md
options.why: The branch never touched config.yaml. Different files cannot clash.

feedback.correct: Same or touching lines conflict; separated lines merge cleanly.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask whether the two edits touch, line by line.

explain.text: git merges line by line. Edits to the same line, or to touching lines with nothing unchanged between them, form one clash. Edits with an untouched line between them merge cleanly.

items.prose: Yesterday's commit on main doubled the position size by mistake. Two colleagues have built branches on it since.
items.question: How do you undo it?

options.why: Their branches still contain the commit. Rewinding main makes the histories disagree, and it returns when they merge.
The mistake is committed. restore only discards uncommitted edits.
Their work is theirs. Deleting labels does not make a rewrite safe.

feedback.correct: revert adds a cancelling commit and rewrites nothing.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Others already have the commit.

explain.text: Once others have a commit, add to history rather than rewrite it. `git revert` makes a new commit that halves the position again. Everyone's history still agrees.

items.prose: On main at c3 you ran `git branch carry`, then committed c4. The commit landed on main, and carry still points at c3. Nobody else has c4. You want c4 on carry and main back on c3.
items.question: Put the commands in order.

lines.text: `git merge main`, a fast-forward to c4

feedback.correct: carry catches up to c4, then main steps back to c3.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Make sure something still reaches c4 before main lets go of it.

byKey.reset: You moved main back first. Nothing would reach c4 any more, so carry could not pick it up.
byKey.back: You went back to main before carry had caught up.
byKey.merge: Merging from main into main does nothing. Switch to carry first.

explain.text: On carry, `git merge main` fast-forwards carry from c3 to c4. Then, on main, `git reset --hard HEAD~1` moves main back to c3. c4 now lives only on carry, as you meant.
